value: more summer-morph flies than winter-morph flies entered traps, even at lower temperatures
eye: antennae and olfactory system (trap-entry behaviour to a food odour)
method: trap-entry behavioural assay in arenas at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 25 C after 72 h acclimation, with standard cornmeal diet (5 mL) as the only odour source; 10 flies released per arena
conditions: female flies of both seasonal morphs; the only odour was cornmeal diet and no concentrations are reported, so no odour threshold or compound identity follows; trap capture rose with temperature and peaked at 25 C; the temperature by morph interaction on trap capture was not significant (chi-square 5.50, df 4, p = 0.239); winter morphs were more active at 0 and 5 C but similar or lower at warmer temperatures, so lower trap entry in winter morphs is not separated from activity; 5 replicates per treatment per morph across three trials (Figure 4 legend says n = 15); the paper's other finding is gene expression (12 olfaction-related genes differing between morphs), not a sensory threshold
